newsitem.title: THAILAND: INTERVIEW - Nortel sees Asia-Pacific growth.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Nortel sees Asia-Pacific growth.

text.p: Leading Canadian telecommunications firm Northern Telecom Ltd (Nortel) said on Wednesday it expected to post further business growth in key Asia-Pacific markets.
"We see Asia-Pacific as very important and our growth rates are very high," James C. Deas, president of Nortel Asia-South Pacific, told Reuters in an interview.
Deas said the firm's Asia-Pacific operations had generated ever-increasing revenue for the group over the past couple of years without showing any signs of slowing.
"Our growth in Asia-Pacific has really come in the last three years. The fast growth is expected to continue over the next few years," he said.

In 1995, Nortel's revenues from the Asia-Pacific and Central and Latin America were up 23 percent to $1.6 billion, or 15 percent of the group's total revenue. Deas gave no revenue figure for the Asia-Pacific region alone.
Nortel's major markets in the region were Australia, the Philippines, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
Deas said his company had positioned Australia as its telecommunications centre for the region.
He also singled out Thailand as an important market because of the country's dynamic and fast-growing economy, and strong need for telecommunications technology.

"We see Thailand as a very important market with a lot of requirement for the advanced telecommunications technology," he said. "Its market also has an increasing number of operators, more competition."

Nortel on Wednesday was awarded a contract worth $200 million by local mobile telephone operator Wireless Communication Services Co Ltd. Under the deal, Nortel will supply digital mobile telephone switching and transmission equipment to the Thai firm.
Deas said the contract, which is the Nortel's largest telecommunications deal in Thailand, would strengthen the company's presence in the country.
